facts.fact: The Winter Crossing Law sets the bound rope at eight spans of the guide's own arm (what one guide can hold on a slide). The spirit limit stays twelve arm-spans (F008); Rohan says so, and Ila jokes that someone should measure the jogini's twelve. This supersedes F263's twelve for the law.

Rohan's night promise 'I will stay' makes the rope hum low and level, felt by both of them (applies F149). His 'I do not mean to abuse the call' is stated as belief, not a vow, and the rope stays silent.
At the Garh Neshar gate Kiran, too weak for the road, stands silent in his blanket with a hand on his torn ear, and stays with Ila (sets up F272, F273).
Hakam's cousin, the winter Meera was nineteen, is the first person in her count; the second is his wife.
A Neshar post stands on the road back toward Shilak; its guards pass the writ after one look at the seal.
